tagline: RF measurement, modeling, and documentation of terrain propagation phenomena in Colorado.

research.title: Dual-Band ADS-B Receive Station
research.subtitle: 978 / 1090 MHz — Permanent Installation
research.summary: Permanent two-antenna receive station on metal garage roof south of Fountain, CO. Long-term ADS-B coverage data to study Front Range terrain propagation asymmetry.
research.description: Permanent two-antenna receive station on metal garage roof south of Fountain, CO. Continuous long-term ADS-B coverage data collection to study Front Range terrain propagation asymmetry. This installation provides empirical data on how mountainous terrain affects signal coverage at aviation frequencies.
research.meta: Location: Fountain, CO | Frequencies: 978 MHz / 1090 MHz | Status: Operational

research.title: Co-Siting Analysis of a Dual-Band ADS-B Receive Station
research.subtitle: Maxwell to Far-Field Integral Equations
research.summary: Analytical co-siting study. Elevation patterns from Maxwell's equations. FlightAware collinear reverse-engineered as N=4 elements. FM band is binding isolation constraint.
research.description: Analytical co-siting study deriving elevation patterns from Maxwell's equations. FlightAware collinear antenna reverse-engineered as N=4 element array. FM broadcast band identified as binding isolation constraint. Extended with HFSS full-wave cross-validation for submission to ARRL QEX magazine.
research.meta: Approach: Analytical + HFSS FDTD | Target: ARRL QEX | Expected: Q4 2026

research.title: Terrestrial Analog Modeling of VHF Propagation
research.subtitle: 88.33 Miles — The 88-Mile Challenge
research.summary: Inaugural FRRRI field study across Rampart Range terrain obstacle (7,000–9,000 ft). Path loss exceeding 110 dB. Reviewed by Dr. Paul Wilkinson, SIEEE.
research.description: Inaugural FRRRI field study. Lookout Mountain to Pikes Peak International Raceway across 7,000–9,000 ft terrain obstacle. Path loss exceeding 110 dB at 99.5 MHz. Demonstrates extreme terrain diffraction in Front Range geometry. Reviewed by Dr. Paul Wilkinson, SIEEE.
research.meta: Distance: 88.33 miles | Frequency: 99.5 MHz | Obstacle: 7,000–9,000 ft | Published: 2026
